### `shopping_mall_ai_coupons`

Core business table representing all platform and seller-issued coupons.
Defines coupon metadata, scope, state, issuance/redeem conditions, quota,
source campaign, stackability policy, and issuance controls. Tied to
issuance/redemption logs and parent campaigns. Supports both
product-level and cart-level discount logic. Links to campaign and
optionally a seller or platform administrator. Follows snapshot and
compliance/auditing patterns. Used extensively in coupon event flows.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key.
- `shopping_mall_ai_discount_campaign_id`
  > Source discount campaign's {@link
  > shopping_mall_ai_discount_campaigns.id}. References the campaign that
  > originated this coupon.
- `shopping_mall_ai_seller_id`
  > Coupon's issuing seller's [shopping_mall_ai_sellers.id](#shopping_mall_ai_sellers). Nullable
  > if platform-wide or administrator coupon.
- `shopping_mall_ai_administrator_id`
  > Coupon's issuing administrator's {@link
  > shopping_mall_ai_administrators.id}. Nullable if seller coupon.
- `code`: Coupon code (unique per platform or per campaign, used for redemption).
- `title`: Coupon display title/purpose (e.g. Spring Sale 10%).
- `description`: Detailed description of the coupon offer or campaign.
- `type`
  > Type of coupon (fixed, percent, free_shipping) for platform logic.
  > Limited to allowed enums in business logic.
- `scope`: Scope of coupon applicability (e.g., product, category, cart-wide).
- `status`
  > Current state: issued, active, suspended, expired, redeemed, revoked,
  > deleted. Life-cycle management for backend enforcement.
- `issued_quantity`: Total number of coupon codes issued. Used for quota and tracking.
- `issued_per_user_quota`: Redemption quota per unique user. Used for eligibility checks.
- `redeemed_quantity`
  > Number of times this coupon has been redeemed. For quota and abuse
  > monitoring.
- `max_discount_amount`
  > Cap (if any) on discount value this coupon can grant. Applies to
  > percent/fixed.
- `minimum_purchase_amount`: Minimum order value for coupon applicability.
- `start_at`: Coupon enable/start date.
- `end_at`: Coupon expiration/end date. Used for redemption window.
- `stackable`
  > Whether this coupon can be stacked/combined with others in a single
  > purchase.
- `created_at`: Record creation timestamp.
- `updated_at`: Record update timestamp.
- `deleted_at`: Soft delete timestamp (null if not deleted).

### `shopping_mall_ai_coupon_issuance_logs`

Immutable audit log for every coupon issuance event, associating a coupon
to a particular user, including issuance method, status, quantities, and
actor. Used for quota, abuse, and compliance tracking. Enables detailed
analytics and abuse investigations. Never directly updated except for
rare administrative correction.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key.
- `shopping_mall_ai_coupon_id`: Issued coupon's [shopping_mall_ai_coupons.id](#shopping_mall_ai_coupons).
- `shopping_mall_ai_customer_id`
  > Target customer's [shopping_mall_ai_customers.id](#shopping_mall_ai_customers) (recipient of the
  > issued coupon).
- `issued_at`: Issuance timestamp for audit.
- `issued_by_ip`: IP address from which the issuance originated. For security and audit.
- `method`: Issuance method (automatic, admin, seller, event, bulk, API, etc.).
- `quantity`
  > Number of coupons granted in this event. Typically 1, but supports bulk
  > issuance.
- `notes`: Issuance-related admin/seller notes. Optional audit/context field.
- `created_at`: Record creation timestamp.

### `shopping_mall_ai_coupon_redemption_logs`

Immutable log for coupon redemption activity, linking issued coupon code
to a user, order, and redemption context. Enforces 1:1 relationship for
single-use coupons, supports multiple redemptions for multi-use where
business policy allows. Used for auditing, quota, fraud, and analytics.
All state changes are temporal, with immutable logs.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key.
- `shopping_mall_ai_coupon_id`: Redeemed coupon's [shopping_mall_ai_coupons.id](#shopping_mall_ai_coupons).
- `shopping_mall_ai_customer_id`
  > The customer's [shopping_mall_ai_customers.id](#shopping_mall_ai_customers) who redeemed the
  > coupon.
- `shopping_mall_ai_order_id`
  > Order's [shopping_mall_ai_orders.id](#shopping_mall_ai_orders) to which the coupon was
  > applied.
- `redeemed_at`: Date and time of coupon redemption.
- `status`
  > Redemption result/state (success, failed, reversed, abuse_suspected,
  > etc.).
- `discount_amount`: Discount value granted by this redemption event.
- `notes`: Redemption-related admin/automation notes.
- `created_at`: Record creation timestamp.

### `shopping_mall_ai_discount_campaigns`

Master table for all discount and coupon campaigns (both platform and
seller-scope). Defines campaign metadata, rule sets, status, campaign
window, organizer, and analytic properties. Manages groupings of coupons
and core restrictions, such as issuance policy, eligible channels, quota,
and business objectives. Enables extensible marketing and multi-seller
campaign management.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key.
- `shopping_mall_ai_administrator_id`
  > Campaign's owning administrator's {@link
  > shopping_mall_ai_administrators.id}. Nullable if seller-driven.
- `shopping_mall_ai_seller_id`
  > Campaign's owning seller's [shopping_mall_ai_sellers.id](#shopping_mall_ai_sellers). Nullable
  > if platform only.
- `name`: Campaign official name (unique within marketing domain).
- `description`: Detailed description of campaign purpose and target audience.
- `status`
  > Current status: draft, active, ended, archived, suspended. Used for
  > campaign workflow.
- `budget_amount`
  > Optional campaign budget for analytic/audit. Relevant for cost-based
  > campaigns.
- `total_coupon_quantity`: Total maximum number of coupons issued by this campaign.
- `start_at`: Campaign start date for timing logic.
- `end_at`: Campaign end/expiration date.
- `created_at`: Record creation timestamp.
- `updated_at`: Record update timestamp.
- `deleted_at`: Soft delete/archival timestamp. Null if active.

### `shopping_mall_ai_discount_rules`

Extensible table defining discount/coupon eligibility, stacking, and
application business logic. Specifies product, category, channel,
section, quota, amount, and constraints, including exclusion and stacking
priority. Ties to campaigns and optionally coupons for granular
targeting. Used for automated discount engine rule evaluation and
enforcement.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key.
- `shopping_mall_ai_discount_campaign_id`: Parent campaign's [shopping_mall_ai_discount_campaigns.id](#shopping_mall_ai_discount_campaigns).
- `shopping_mall_ai_coupon_id`
  > Related coupon's [shopping_mall_ai_coupons.id](#shopping_mall_ai_coupons) if this rule maps to
  > a specific coupon.
- `shopping_mall_ai_section_id`
  > Target section's [shopping_mall_ai_sections.id](#shopping_mall_ai_sections) for rule
  > application. Optional granularity for complex sales.
- `shopping_mall_ai_channel_id`
  > Target channel's [shopping_mall_ai_channels.id](#shopping_mall_ai_channels). Nullable for
  > platform-scope.
- `shopping_mall_ai_category_id`
  > Target category's [shopping_mall_ai_categories.id](#shopping_mall_ai_categories). Nullable if
  > discounts are not category-specific.
- `shopping_mall_ai_product_id`
  > Target product's [shopping_mall_ai_products.id](#shopping_mall_ai_products). Nullable if rule
  > applies more broadly.
- `rule_type`
  > Type of rule (eligibility, exclusion, stacking, amount, quota, window,
  > etc.). For discount engine logic segmentation.
- `application_type`: How the rule is applied (product, cart, channel, etc.).
- `amount_type`: Type of amount (fixed, percent, free_shipping, etc.).
- `amount_value`
  > Discount value specified by the rule (fixed value or percent as context
  > implies).
- `minimum_purchase_amount`: Minimum order amount required for rule validity.
- `maximum_discount_amount`: Maximum cap on discount granted by this rule. Applies to percent rules.
- `stack_priority`: Order precedence for stacking enforcement/priority.
- `quota`: Redemption quota limit for this rule.
- `start_at`: Rule activation/start datetime.
- `end_at`: Rule deactivation/end datetime.
- `created_at`: Record creation timestamp.
- `updated_at`: Record update timestamp.
- `deleted_at`: Soft delete timestamp (null if active or never deleted).

### `shopping_mall_ai_deposit_accounts`

Represents the balance deposit account for each customer. Tracks all
in-app refundable deposit (cash-equivalent) per user. Each customer has
one unique deposit account. All balance updates (credits/debits) are
tracked via [shopping_mall_ai_deposit_transactions](#shopping_mall_ai_deposit_transactions).

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key.
- `shopping_mall_ai_customer_id`
  > Belonged customer's [shopping_mall_ai_customers.id](#shopping_mall_ai_customers). The owner of
  > this deposit account.
- `balance`
  > Current deposit account balance (cash-equivalent, withdrawable). Updated
  > only by transaction history application.
- `status`
  > Logical status of the deposit account (e.g., active, frozen, closed) -
  > for compliance and support operations.
- `created_at`: Deposit account creation timestamp.
- `updated_at`: Last update timestamp for deposit account.
- `deleted_at`: Soft deletion timestamp, null if active.

### `shopping_mall_ai_mileage_accounts`

Mileage (platform point) account for each customer. Each customer holds
one mileage account to manage all point-based reward balance. Updated
through [shopping_mall_ai_mileage_transactions](#shopping_mall_ai_mileage_transactions). Identifies owner
by customer FK for integrity.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key.
- `shopping_mall_ai_customer_id`
  > Belonged customer's [shopping_mall_ai_customers.id](#shopping_mall_ai_customers). The owner of
  > this mileage account.
- `balance`
  > Current mileage (platform points) balance. Updated only through
  > transaction history application.

- `updated_at`: Last update timestamp for this mileage account.

polymorphic), affected model/table, before/after values (as JSON),
rationale, and precise timestamps. Covers all business-impacting
financial actions.

  > Acting seller's [shopping_mall_ai_sellers.id](#shopping_mall_ai_sellers), if initiated by
  > seller. Polymorphic role support; nullable.

  > Name of affected table/model (e.g., shopping_mall_ai_deposit_accounts,
  > shopping_mall_ai_mileage_transactions, etc.).
- `target_id`: UUID of affected business record (PK of target).
- `action_type`
  > Type of action/event audited (e.g., create, update, delete,
  > manual_adjust, refund, etc.).
- `before_value`
  > JSON snapshot of value before change. Business context for auditability.
  > Nullable for create actions.
- `after_value`
  > JSON snapshot of value after change. Business audit value for trace,
  > nullable for delete actions.
- `rationale`
  > Human-readable rationale/comments for this audit entry (nullable, for
  > manual justification or policy context).
- `created_at`: Timestamp when the audit log was recorded.

### `shopping_mall_ai_reviews`

Stores primary product/service review content submitted by customers.
Each review references the product being reviewed, the author, and
optionally, related orders or sellers. Supports full-text search,
auditability, and drives user reputation features. Snapshots are stored
separately in shopping_mall_ai_review_snapshots. Links to moderation logs
for compliance. Only one review per customer and product per order is
allowed.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key.
- `shopping_mall_ai_customer_id`: Author customer's [shopping_mall_ai_customers.id](#shopping_mall_ai_customers).
- `shopping_mall_ai_product_id`: Target product's [shopping_mall_ai_products.id](#shopping_mall_ai_products).
- `shopping_mall_ai_order_id`
  > Order context (if review is post-purchase), references {@link
  > shopping_mall_ai_orders.id}.
- `title`: Review headline/title. Free text, max 255 characters.
- `body`: Main review content body. Rich text or markdown allowed.
- `rating`: Rating score (e.g., 1–5).
- `visible`
  > Whether the review is visible to the public. Changes as result of
  > moderation.
- `reported`: Whether this review has been reported for moderation investigation.
- `created_at`: Creation timestamp.
- `updated_at`: Last update timestamp.
- `deleted_at`: Soft delete timestamp if review is logically deleted.

### `shopping_mall_ai_review_snapshots`

Historical immutable snapshots of all reviews for legal, audit, and
rollback purposes. Used to preserve every edit or deletion. Each snapshot
records review state at change time, references the original review, and
the editor (usually the author or a moderator). No updates after
creation. Enables full legal audit, compliance, and rollback/restoration
logic.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key.
- `shopping_mall_ai_review_id`: Source review's [shopping_mall_ai_reviews.id](#shopping_mall_ai_reviews).
- `shopping_mall_ai_customer_id`
  > The actor who made the edit (author or moderator), references {@link
  > shopping_mall_ai_customers.id}.
- `snapshot_action`
  > Type of action causing snapshot (created, edited, deleted, restored,
  > moderated, etc.).
- `title`: Review title at time of snapshot.
- `body`: Review body content at time of snapshot.
- `rating`: Rating score at change time.
- `visible`: Visibility flag at time of snapshot.
- `reported`: Reported flag at time of snapshot.
- `created_at`: Snapshot creation time.

### `shopping_mall_ai_inquiries`

Stores customer and seller inquiries, tickets, or messages about
products, orders, or general service. Each inquiry references the author
(customer or seller) and optionally the related product, order, or
seller. Used for customer service, dispute resolution, and audit.
Supports full-text search and multi-role workflows. Snapshots stored
separately.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key.
- `author_customer_id`
  > Author customer's [shopping_mall_ai_customers.id](#shopping_mall_ai_customers). Nullable if
  > inquiry is by a seller.
- `author_seller_id`
  > Author seller's [shopping_mall_ai_sellers.id](#shopping_mall_ai_sellers). Nullable if inquiry
  > is by a customer.
- `shopping_mall_ai_product_id`: Target product's [shopping_mall_ai_products.id](#shopping_mall_ai_products).
- `shopping_mall_ai_order_id`: Associated order's [shopping_mall_ai_orders.id](#shopping_mall_ai_orders).
- `subject`: Inquiry subject line or title. Free text, up to 255 characters.
- `body`: Full inquiry message body. May be rich text/markdown.
- `status`: Current status (open, closed, escalated, etc.).
- `visible`: Whether the inquiry is visible to general users or only to admins/seller.
- `has_evidence`: Indicates presence of attached evidence (files, screenshots, etc.).
- `created_at`: Creation timestamp.
- `updated_at`: Last update timestamp.
- `deleted_at`: Soft delete timestamp if inquiry is logically deleted.

### `shopping_mall_ai_inquiry_snapshots`

Historical immutable snapshots of all inquiries for full audit trail and
evidence. Captures all changes for dispute or compliance. Each snapshot
is bound to the original inquiry and action initiator (author or
moderator). No updates permitted after creation. Used for legal
restoration or review audits.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key.
- `shopping_mall_ai_inquiry_id`: Source inquiry's [shopping_mall_ai_inquiries.id](#shopping_mall_ai_inquiries).
- `actor_customer_id`

  > shopping_mall_ai_customers.id}. Nullable if made by a seller.
- `actor_seller_id`
  > The actor seller if edit/moderation is by a seller, references {@link
  > shopping_mall_ai_sellers.id}. Nullable if made by a customer.
- `snapshot_action`: Action leading to snapshot (created, edited, deleted, moderated, etc.).
- `subject`: Inquiry subject at time of snapshot.
- `body`: Inquiry body/content at time of snapshot.
- `status`: Inquiry status at time of edit.
- `visible`: Visibility flag at time of edit.
- `has_evidence`: Whether evidence was attached at this point.
- `created_at`: Snapshot creation timestamp.

### `shopping_mall_ai_comments`

Stores replies and threaded comments on reviews or inquiries. Enables
two-level threading (1 reply per role), supports moderation and full
evidence chain. Comments can attach evidence (files), and have
soft-delete. Every edit or deletion is snapshotted. Used for
transparency, compliance, and community features.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key.

- `shopping_mall_ai_inquiry_id`

  > on inquiry). Nullable if not applicable.
- `parent_id`: Parent comment (for threaded replies). Nullable for top-level comments.
- `author_customer_id`
  > Comment author's customer ID, referencing {@link
  > shopping_mall_ai_customers.id}. Nullable if seller/admin.
- `author_seller_id`
  > Comment author's seller ID, referencing {@link
  > shopping_mall_ai_sellers.id}. Nullable if customer/admin.
- `author_administrator_id`
  > Comment author's administrator ID, referencing {@link
  > shopping_mall_ai_administrators.id}. Nullable if customer/seller.
- `body`: Comment content body. Rich text or markdown.
- `has_evidence`: Whether evidence (file) is attached.
- `visible`: Whether the comment is visible to the public.
- `created_at`: Comment creation time.
- `updated_at`: Last update timestamp.
- `deleted_at`: Soft delete timestamp if comment is logically deleted.

### `shopping_mall_ai_comment_snapshots`

Snapshots all historical versions of comments for audit, moderation,
rollback, or legal defense. Immutable after creation. Each snapshot is
associated with the original comment and actor. Used for transparency and
evidence preservation.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key.
- `shopping_mall_ai_comment_id`: Source comment's [shopping_mall_ai_comments.id](#shopping_mall_ai_comments).
- `actor_customer_id`: Snapshot actor (customer); nullable for moderators/admins/sellers.
- `actor_seller_id`: Snapshot actor (seller); nullable for other roles.
- `actor_administrator_id`: Snapshot actor (administrator); nullable for other roles.
- `snapshot_action`: Action type (created, edited, deleted, moderated, restored, etc.)
- `body`: Comment body as in this version.
- `has_evidence`: Whether evidence was present in this version.
- `visible`: Visibility flag at the time of the version.
- `created_at`: Snapshot creation timestamp.

### `shopping_mall_ai_moderation_logs`

Moderation and admin audit log for all review, inquiry, or comment
moderation actions. Stores who, what, when, and why for legal/evidence
purposes. Covers escalations, approvals, rejections, auto-moderation,
sanctions, and dispute resolution. Used for audit trail, legal
compliance, measuring moderation velocity, and repeated offense
analytics. Each entity type subject to moderation will be referenced
optionally by non-null FK.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key.
- `moderator_administrator_id`
  > Administrator/moderator performing the action, references {@link
  > shopping_mall_ai_administrators.id}.
- `shopping_mall_ai_review_id`: Target review for moderation (nullable if not applicable).
- `shopping_mall_ai_inquiry_id`: Target inquiry for moderation (nullable if not applicable).
- `shopping_mall_ai_comment_id`: Target comment for moderation (nullable if not applicable).
- `moderation_action`
  > Type of moderation action (approve, reject, hide, sanction, escalate,
  > resolve, etc.).
- `reason`: Business justification or rationale for action.
- `user_note`: Optional note for the affected user (explanation, next steps).
- `created_at`: Timestamp when moderation occurred.

### `shopping_mall_ai_attachments`

Stores metadata and control flags for all uploaded files (attachments),
such as product images, invoices, evidence, or compliance documents. Core
fields include file identification, type, storage URI, business domain
assignment, retention and legal flags, uploader linkage, and access
control hints. Related to shopping_mall_ai_attachment_versions (immutable
versioning) and shopping_mall_ai_attachment_business_links (usage
relationships).

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key.
- `uploaded_by_id`
  > Uploader's ID for polymorphic reference to customer, seller, or
  > administrator. Actual user type to be determined at application logic
  > layer. Refer to shopping_mall_ai_customers, shopping_mall_ai_sellers, or
  > shopping_mall_ai_administrators by id (polymorphic reference, not
  > relational FK).
- `filename`
  > Original file name provided at upload time. Used for audit/history and
  > display purposes.
- `mime_type`: Official MIME type for the attachment (e.g., image/png, application/pdf).
- `file_uri`
  > Internal or CDN-served URI reference to the physical storage location.
  > Retention and compliance policies use this for file retrieval and audit.
- `file_size`: Raw file size in bytes. Used for quota enforcement and monitoring.
- `business_domain`
  > High-level business domain or usage tag for the attachment (e.g.,
  > product_image, invoice, evidence, compliance_doc).
- `retention_policy_code`
  > Code/ID for the retention policy this attachment must follow (e.g.,
  > standard, evidence, regulatory). Controls purge/archival.
- `legal_hold`
  > True if file is under legal hold and cannot be deleted/purged until
  > released by compliance.
- `deleted`
  > True if attachment has been logically deleted or flagged for removal.
  > Soft-delete: retains for audit window.
- `access_acl`
  > Serialized ACL structure (JSON or notation) representing access/control
  > rights for the file. Used for dynamic role-based access checks.
- `created_at`: Attachment creation/upload timestamp (immutable).
- `updated_at`: Timestamp of the last metadata update or audit action for this attachment.
- `deleted_at`
  > Optional timestamp marking when the attachment was flagged as deleted
  > (soft-delete for audit/auditability).

### `shopping_mall_ai_attachment_versions`

Immutable version history for each attachment. Stores all changes,
overwrites, re-uploads, or admin modifications for forensic
chain-of-custody. Each row represents a complete version snapshot,
supporting retrieval, audit, and restoration. References main attachment
and includes all necessary metadata for independent review. Used for
legal and compliance evidence preservation.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key.
- `attachment_id`
  > Parent [shopping_mall_ai_attachments.id](#shopping_mall_ai_attachments) for version chain. All
  > versions of a file are linked to the original attachment ID.
- `modified_by_id`
  > Modifier's ID for polymorphic reference to customer, seller, or
  > administrator. Actual user type to be determined at application logic
  > layer. Must be one of shopping_mall_ai_customers,
  > shopping_mall_ai_sellers, or shopping_mall_ai_administrators by id
  > (polymorphic reference, not relational FK).
- `version_number`
  > Monotonic version number for the attachment (1 = original, incremented
  > per version/change).
- `file_uri`
  > URI of the actual file storage location for this version (past versions
  > may be archived elsewhere).
- `file_size`
  > File size (in bytes) for this specific version (may differ from
  > current/file).
- `created_at`: Timestamp when this version was created/uploaded.
- `diff_comment`
  > Free-text or system note describing the difference versus the prior
  > version (e.g., who/why/what changed).
- `deleted`
  > True if this version is logically deleted or excluded (rare; usually only
  > on redaction/legal action).

### `shopping_mall_ai_attachment_business_links`

Links attachments to arbitrary business records for joinless queries.
Each row binds an attachment to a single business domain/entity (e.g.,
products, invoices, reviews, orders). Ensures referential integrity,
supports full chain of custody, and allows for future extension to new
modules without migration, using polymorphic target identification.
Essential for content display, evidence trails, and legal audit.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key.
- `attachment_id`
  > Attachment [shopping_mall_ai_attachments.id](#shopping_mall_ai_attachments) linked to this
  > business entity.
- `target_domain`
  > Business domain type/category for the link (e.g., product, order, review,
  > evidence, seller_doc, compliance).
- `target_id`
  > UUID of the linked business entity in its respective domain (e.g.,
  > shopping_mall_ai_products.id, shopping_mall_ai_orders.id, etc.).
  > Polymorphic by target_domain.
- `linked_by_id`
  > User [shopping_mall_ai_customers.id](#shopping_mall_ai_customers), {@link
  > shopping_mall_ai_sellers.id}, or {@link
  > shopping_mall_ai_administrators.id} who created the link.
- `created_at`: Timestamp when the business link was created.

### `shopping_mall_ai_ai_reco_signals`

Logs all AI-powered recommendation engine signals, including event type,
triggering context (user, product, session), recommendations served,
recipient, feedback/interaction outcome, and related AI model metadata.
Enables tracing recommendation effectiveness, user response (CTR,
conversion, ignore), and supports feedback loop for continuous AI model
learning. High-volume, temporal, mission-critical for analytics and
product improvement.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key.
- `shopping_mall_ai_customer_id`
  > Belonged customer's [shopping_mall_ai_customers.id](#shopping_mall_ai_customers). References the
  > recipient of the recommendation signal.
- `shopping_mall_ai_product_id`
  > Optional referenced [shopping_mall_ai_products.id](#shopping_mall_ai_products) for
  > product-centric recommendations.
- `signal_type`
  > Type of AI recommendation event (e.g., 'home_reco', 'personalized_top5',
  > 'similar_product', etc.).
- `input_data`
  > JSON string capturing input/context fed into the recommendation engine at
  > trigger time (could include preferences, search state, etc.).
- `output_recommendation`
  > JSON string representing recommendations produced (product ids, scores,
  > explanation, rank).
- `feedback_type`
  > Type of user feedback/interaction (e.g., 'clicked', 'purchased',
  > 'ignored', 'hidden', etc.).
- `ai_model_version`: Deployed model/version identifier used to generate this recommendation.
- `session_id`: Session or event correlation id, for tracing user/context lifecycle.
- `created_at`: Time the recommendation signal/event was logged.
- `updated_at`
  > Timestamp of last update to this signal record (for corrections, feedback
  > propagation, etc).

### `shopping_mall_ai_ai_personalization_profiles`

Per-user AI personalization/segmentation profile. Maintains long-lived,
explainable analytics about user's preferences, affinity
vectors/features, cluster/segment assignment, opt-outs, and important
model explainability factors. Updated on profile-triggering events and
batch AI processing. Enables highly targeted experiences, responsible AI,
and rollbacks.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key.
- `shopping_mall_ai_customer_id`
  > Belonged customer's [shopping_mall_ai_customers.id](#shopping_mall_ai_customers). References the
  > subject of the profile.
- `profile_type`: Type of profile (e.g., 'profile_v1', 'segment_v2', 'contextual', etc.).
- `affinity_vector`
  > AI-generated vector or JSON summary of user preferences/features
  > (stringified for flexibility).
- `segment_label`
  > Current segment or group assigned by AI (e.g., 'fashion_enthusiast',
  > 'tech_buyer').
- `exclusions`: Serialized exclusions (brands, categories) opted out of personalization.
- `explainability_json`: Explainability/interpretability model results in JSON.
- `last_update_source`: What triggered the last update (event type, batch, admin).
- `updated_at`: Latest profile update time.
- `created_at`: Profile creation timestamp.

### `shopping_mall_ai_ai_analytics_exposures`

Tracks analytic/experiment/feature exposure events, logging who/what was
shown, group/variant, context, exposure metadata (e.g., AI campaign,
test, or algorithm). Critical for A/B test analysis, campaign
attribution, model governance and privacy log requirements. Supports
business/statistical analytics and audit.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key.
- `shopping_mall_ai_customer_id`
  > Belonged customer's [shopping_mall_ai_customers.id](#shopping_mall_ai_customers). References
  > exposed subject for analytics.
- `exposure_type`
  > Nature of exposure (e.g., 'AI_campaign', 'ab_test',
  > 'recommendation_algo').
- `exposure_context`
  > Serialized JSON context of exposure (e.g., what was shown, parameters,
  > features).
- `group_assignment`: Variant or group id for bucket analysis ('A', 'B', 'control', etc.).
- `exposure_metadata`: Any additional metadata re: exposure type, test conditions, etc. (JSON).
- `result_outcome`
  > Post-exposure response or outcome, for effect attribution. (e.g., click,
  > conversion, bounce).
- `created_at`: When the exposure occurred/logged.

### `shopping_mall_ai_ai_price_optimizations`

Records of all AI-driven (or heuristic) price optimization events, such
as suggestions, updates, campaign-triggered changes, and final
acceptance. Linked to time, product, channel, suggestion metadata, and
campaign context. Stores rationale, output, acceptance by operators, and
actual result (if known). Enables pricing science, campaign and model
tuning analytics, regulatory/compliance evidence.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key.
- `shopping_mall_ai_product_id`
  > Targeted product's [shopping_mall_ai_products.id](#shopping_mall_ai_products). References the
  > product for which a price optimization event occurred.
- `optimization_type`
  > Type/purpose of price optimization (e.g., 'AI_suggestion',
  > 'manual_intervention', 'campaign', 'regulatory_correction').
- `channel_id`
  > Channel/store/campaign context in which the optimization was performed
  > (if multi-channel).
- `original_price`: Original product price before optimization event.
- `suggested_price`: Price suggested by AI/model/campaign, etc.
- `final_price`: Final price actually applied (may differ from suggestion).
- `decision_rationale`
  > Serialized JSON documenting explanation/justification (regulatory, model,
  > business) for optimization.
- `accepted_by`: Who/what accepted the suggestion (user id, automated, override, etc.).
- `result_outcome`
  > Final observed result/impact (if measured) - e.g., conversion uplift,
  > inventory move, complaint, rollback.
- `created_at`: Timestamp of price optimization event.
- `updated_at`: Timestamp last updated (correction, outcome update, etc.).

### `shopping_mall_ai_fraud_logs`

Specialized event/incident log capturing AI/heuristics-driven fraud/risk
scoring, intervention triggers (e.g., high-risk behaviors, payment
anomalies), and final actions (blocks, holds, escalations). Each row
records all primary signal properties, reasoning, action, and business
outcome. Used for risk analytics, compliance, fraud audits, and tuning of
AI risk models.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key.
- `shopping_mall_ai_customer_id`: Optional involved customer's [shopping_mall_ai_customers.id](#shopping_mall_ai_customers).
- `shopping_mall_ai_order_id`: Order context (if relevant): [shopping_mall_ai_orders.id](#shopping_mall_ai_orders).
- `fraud_signal_type`
  > Type/category of fraud/risk indicator (e.g., 'multi_failed_login',
  > 'stolen_card', 'geolocation_mismatch', etc.).
- `risk_score`: Quantitative fraud/risk score produced by AI/model/heuristic analysis.
- `detail_json`
  > JSON-serialized input/behavior/data (IP, device, location, context, etc)
  > for root cause/evidence.
- `intervention_type`
  > Action taken due to risk/fraud (e.g., 'soft_block', 'order_hold',
  > 'user_alert', 'system_lock', etc.)
- `final_outcome`
  > Result of fraud incident investigation (e.g., 'auto_resolved',
  > 'escalated', 'cleared', 'blocked').
- `created_at`: Timestamp of fraud detection/incident logged.

### `shopping_mall_ai_incident_logs`

Business-level, centralized incident log for exceptions, anomalies,
business rule violations, workflow failures, errors, or escalated
security/AI/fraud events not captured in domain-specific logs. Includes
context, trigger source, actors, impact, timeline, affected objects,
timeline/status, and resolution. Key for regulatory, operational, and
cross-domain audit/compliance.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key.
- `shopping_mall_ai_customer_id`
  > Associated customer if relevant. Optional link to {@link
  > shopping_mall_ai_customers.id}.
- `incident_type`
  > Type/category of incident (e.g., 'AI_runtime_error', 'workflow_failure',
  > 'policy_violation', 'escalated_support', 'security_flag', etc).
- `incident_context`: Serialized JSON context and trigger snapshot.
- `status`
  > Current status of incident resolution (e.g., 'open', 'in_review',
  > 'escalated', 'resolved', 'closed').
- `impact_level`
  > Freeform impact classification (e.g., 'none', 'minor', 'business',
  > 'data_loss', 'legal', etc).
- `actor`
  > Who/what triggered or is responsible for the incident (user id, system,
  > AI, admin, etc).
- `resolution_summary`: Description/summary of resolution, mitigation, or update.
- `created_at`: When the incident was logged/created.
- `updated_at`: When this incident record was last updated (status, resolution).

### `shopping_mall_ai_audit_trails`

Long-term, full-fidelity audit log for all AI-driven and
business-critical actions/decisions/changes affecting major business
objects (user, product, order, payment, model, pricing, access, etc).
Immutable, actor/timestamp/event/target cross-referenced. Essential for
compliance, root-cause, incident investigation, and regulatory/legal
discovery.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key.
- `shopping_mall_ai_customer_id`
  > Subject/affected customer, if any. References {@link
  > shopping_mall_ai_customers.id}.
- `event_type`
  > Type/category of audit event (e.g., 'ai_action', 'data_edit',
  > 'access_grant', 'fraud_flag', 'model_update').
- `target_type`
  > What was affected by this event (e.g., 'product', 'order', 'user',
  > 'model', 'pricing').
- `target_id`: Business identifier (UUID or business id) of the affected object.
- `actor`: Who/what performed/triggered this action (user id, system, admin, AI).
- `data_before`
  > Serialized (JSON) snapshot of object state before change/event, or null
  > if not applicable.
- `data_after`
  > Serialized (JSON) snapshot of object state after change/event, or null if
  > not applicable.
- `description`: Free-form business explanation of what happened, why (for compliance).
- `created_at`: Audit event timestamp.
